original.text: de phyir 'jig rten brtags pa'i tha snyad rnal 'byor lam 'dir mi dgos so/
original.edition: Derge Tengyur (sde dge bstan 'gyur), digital edition by Esukhia and Barom Theksum Choling, Tōh 2591; Wylie by the unit (pyewts)
original.licence: Public domain (Derge xylograph; Esukhia/Barom digital edition, per the repository)

paraphrase: This path of the great sage is subtle and hard to know: non-conceptual, beyond conceptions, hard to examine and to teach, free of verbal convention and not within the reach of the immature — one looks to the Teacher's definitive scripture and the instructions of holy masters. Analysis that takes perception and the like as valid means follows an endless stream of conceptions and cannot reach the essence; therefore the worldly conventions of examination are not needed on this yogic path.
speaker: Mañjuśrīmitra
notes: Passage located and read in the local Derge e-text (folio in location.section); paraphrase by U45 from the Tibetan (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked).

paraphrase: Those deceived by conceptions, following the stream of delusion like dreamers taking dreams as true, who abandon this path and teach other paths as the unmistaken one, are like gold in ore — worthy of compassion. May this unsurpassed non-dual path, established by valid means through the power of familiarity, spread for the benefit of beings.
speaker: Mañjuśrīmitra
notes: Passage located and read in the local Derge e-text (folio in location.section); paraphrase by U45 from the Tibetan (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked). The phrase 'rdo la gser bzhin' (like gold in ore) gives the text its Tibetan name.
